summary: Add the §5.9 (C5) CertifiedPatch implementation for the landed bilinear CoonsSurface as a NEW truck-certified kernel module (orphan-rule placement): vendor/truck/truck-certified/src/kernel/coons_patch.rs implements enclose/derivs/normal_cone/regularity/weight_bound for CoonsSurface<C: ParametricCurve3D> over the recovered cached corners p00..p11 via product-form CertifiedInterval arithmetic in the N2-pinned evaluation orders (enclose expands ((1-u)(1-v)p00 + u(1-v)p10) + ((1-u)v p01 + u v p11) per coordinate; derivs use the once-hand-differentiated bilinear partials S_u = (1-v)(p10-p00) + v(p11-p01), S_v = (1-u)(p01-p00) + u(p11-p10); regularity classifies the exposed EG-F^2 against config::TOL_JACOBIAN with the Proven/Disproven/Inconclusive split; weight_bound returns the frozen §3.1 constant-1 Proven plumbing; the §5.9 one-call rule is exposed as pub egf2 for the machine-check). No change to CoonsSurface itself (V5 identity). New tests/kernel_coons_patch.rs carries the six required machine-checked ground truths (BG-KV2-205-C5PATCH).

details: 1: CoonsSurface stored fields/constructors MATCH the census — truck-geometry/src/decorators/coons.rs stores bottom/top/left/right plus cached corners p00/p10/p01/p11, try_new validates the four corner equalities pairwise at DirectTolerance::default().position and caches p00=bottom(0), p10=bottom(1), p01=top(0), p11=top(1); no deviation, no stop.

2: the bilinear interval form proves regularity on the regular (twisted) fixture with wide margin — over box [0.4,0.4]x[0.6,0.6] the certified EG-F^2 lower bound is ~0.51, five orders above the 1e-12 TOL_JACOBIAN floor (Proven, no loosening); the full-unit-box interval evaluation is dependency-widened to Inconclusive, which is the certified-subdivision behavior documented in-module, not a proof failure.

notes: A4 is a dispatch-time anchor: the packet expects grep 'coons_patch' in kernel/mod.rs == 0 at dispatch (module not yet wired). The write set mandates editing kernel/mod.rs to register the module, so after the work the count is exactly 1 (the single `pub mod coons_patch;` line between `config` and `evidence`); recorded as anchors_after for the record.

Certified content is the bilinear Bernstein form over the cached corners p00..p11 (POLYNOMIAL, exact in the corners, no weight field). CoonsSurface's corner fields are private in truck-geometry, so the impl recovers them deterministically from the stored boundary endpoints through the public accessors: p00 = bottom(0), p10 = bottom(1), p01 = top(0), p11 = top(1) (the constructor caches exactly these). The impl is generic over C: ParametricCurve3D; it is exact (sound) when the four boundary curves are the straight corner segments, which is the C5 recipe geometry — the module doc records that premise so no caller certifies a patch whose boundaries are curved.

Interval evaluation is dependency-widened (product-form CertifiedInterval), so regularity Proven on the regular fixture holds on sub-boxes (e.g. [0.4,0.4]x[0.6,0.6], bound ~0.51) but not on the full unit box; that is the certified-subdivision behavior, matching how the other implementors' regularity is consumed. The folded (bow-tie) fixture is construction-valid and geometry-invalid: at the fold line u=0.5 the exposed Jacobian S_u x S_v vanishes, and regularity over the degenerate center box is Disproven carrying the Degeneracy { box_, egf2 } witness (enclosure below TOL_JACOBIAN); over straddling boxes it is Inconclusive — never Proven.

weight_bound returns Some(Proven(CertifiedPositive(1.0))) over every box — the frozen §3.1 constant-1 plumbing spelled like BG-KV2-104's plane carrier. The one-call rule (spec §5.9) is exposed as pub fn egf2 so the integration test can machine-check that regularity's exact EG-F^2 interval contains the squared magnitude of the landed CoonsSurface::jacobian() f64 cross product at sampled grid points, and that regularity is Proven on every regular sample box.

No transcendental function call appears in the module (machine-checked by no_transcendental_call_in_coons_patch_module, same token list as the leaf/rational scans); normal_cone reuses leaf.rs's closed-hemisphere constructor discipline over the interval cross product of the derivative enclosure.
